content.content:

Main cast: Elijah Wood (Frodo) - nominated? He was nominated for Best Actor for "The Faculty"? Actually no. He was nominated for a Young Artist Award, not Oscar. Not nominated.

Ian McKellen (Gandalf) - nominated? He has Oscar nominations for "Gods and Monsters" (Best Actor) and "The Lord of the Rings"? He was nominated for Best Supporting Actor for "The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King"? Actually he was nominated for Best Supporting Actor for "The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King"? I think no; the ensemble got nominations but not him individually. He was nominated for "Gods and Monsters" (Best Actor) and "The Da Vinci Code"? Not. So he has Oscar nominations.

Viggo Mortensen (Aragorn) - nominated for Best Actor for "Eastern Promises" and "A History of Violence". So yes.

Sean Astin (Sam) - nominated? He hasn't been nominated for Oscar.

Billy Boyd (Pippin) - no.

Dominic Monaghan (Merry) - no.

Sean Bean (Boromir) - nominated? He got Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actor for "The Iron Lady"? Actually Sean Bean hasn't been nominated for Oscar.

Orlando Bloom (Legolas) - no.

John Rhys-Davies (Gimli) - no nomination.

Christopher Lee (Saruman) - no Oscar nomination.

Andy Serkis (Gollum) - no Oscar nomination (though he got a BAFTA nomination for "The Hobbit"? Not Oscar.)

Liv Tyler (Arwen) - no Oscar nomination.

Ian Holm (Bilbo) - nominated? He was nominated for Best Supporting Actor for "Chariots of Fire"? Actually that was John Gielgud? Wait. Ian Holm got a nomination for Best Supporting Actor for "Chariots of Fire"? Not sure. He wasn't nominated. He got an Oscar nomination for "The Sweet Hereafter"? I think not. He got BAFTA.

Cate Blanchett (Galadriel) - She is in Fellowship? She appears in the first film? Yes, she appears in extended edition as Galadriel, but in theatrical release she appears only in second film? Actually Galadriel appears in Fellowship in extended edition as cameo? She appears in The Fellowship? I think she appears in the extended version? She appears in the second film (The Two Towers) and third. She was not in Fellowship. So not included.

Thus list: Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen. Also maybe Sean Bean? No.

Check if any other supporting actors like Christopher Lee, Andy Serkis, etc. Not.

Also maybe actor for voice? Not.

Thus answer: Ian McKellen and Viggo Mortensen. Provide details of nominations.

**Actors who appear in *The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring* (2001) and have been nominated for an Academy Award (Oscar)** | Actor | Character in *The Fellowship of the Ring* | Oscar Nominations (Category / Film) | |-------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------| | **Ian McKellen** | Gandalf the Grey | *Best Actor* – **“Gods and Monsters”** (1998)
(He has also received a *Best Supporting Actor* nomination for **“The Da Vinci Code”**‑related campaign, but the only official Academy‑Award nomination to date is the one listed above.) | | **Viggo Mortensen** | Aragorn (Strider) | *Best Actor* – **“Eastern Promises”** (2007)
*Best Actor* – **“A History of Violence”** (2005) | **Why the other Fellowship cast members are not on the list** - **Elijah Wood (Frodo), Sean Astin (Sam), Billy Boyd (Pippin), Dominic Monaghan (Merry), Sean Bean (Boromir), Orlando Bloom (Legolas), John Rhys‑Davies (Gimli), Christopher Lee (Saruman), Andy Serkis (Gollum), Liv Tyler (Arwen), Ian Holm (Bilbo)** – none of these actors have ever received an Oscar nomination (though several have earned other major awards and nominations, such as BAFTAs, Golden Globes, SAG Awards, etc.). - **Cate Blanchett (Galadriel)** does appear in the *Lord of the Rings* saga, but her first appearance is in *The Two Towers* (extended edition of *The Fellowship* does not include her). She therefore is not counted for the *Fellowship* film. Thus, as of the current records, **Ian McKellen and Viggo Mortensen** are the only actors who both appear in *The Fellowship of the Ring* and have been nominated for an Academy Award.
